page.kicker: System · per server and for all servers
page.infoSub:
All values are stored in the database and apply without a bot restart.
You get IDs in Discord with a right-click → "Copy ID" (developer mode).

permView.areasTip: Who may see or edit which area of the EventHelper
permView.botTip: Who may use which bot command in Discord

page.botCrumb: Access · who may use which bot command in Discord
page.raidChannelSub: The channel a new raid event is created in when none is picked while creating it.
page.raidsheetsSub: Google Sheets by content (tier 4/5 etc.). When filling, the matching sheet is suggested by its keywords. A fixed sheet for a whole raid category is assigned under Categories.
page.topItemsSub: The really big drops — weapons, legendary parts, anything the guild values highly. When a raid awards one of them, the dashboard highlights the award. Which loot addon a category uses is set under Categories.
page.logChannelsSub: Channels where Warcraft Logs are posted automatically. The bot adds the evaluation buttons there.
page.appChannelSub: Channel where new applications are posted as a thread.
page.officerRoleSub: Pinged on new applications. Leave empty for no ping.

gameVersion.mainSub: The default for something new: a category switched on, a new raid template and the raider profile start with it. Existing categories, events and templates keep their version.
gameVersion.categoriesSub: Every active category plays one fixed version. Switching starts a new section: earlier raids, roster and quota stay readable in their version.
gameVersion.noCategories: No active category yet – switch one on under Categories.
gameVersion.hideOthersText: Everybody only sees {version}. {others} disappears from lists, loot, history, roster, catalogue, templates and pickers. Nothing is deleted, switching it off brings everything back.

upcoming.one: There is still 1 upcoming raid of another version ({dates}). It will be hidden but stays reachable through its Discord link – read only.
upcoming.other: There are still {count} upcoming raids of other versions ({dates}). They will be hidden but stay reachable through their Discord link – read only.

gameVersion.exportSub: Loot history and attendance of every version but the main one as a CSV file. Admins only.
gameVersion.preview: This is how the top bar looks
gameVersion.previewOn: Hidden: no switch anymore, only a quiet hint which version is active.
gameVersion.previewOff: Not hidden: everybody can switch between the versions at the top, the choice is remembered per user.

categorySwitch.title: {name}: {from} → {to}
categorySwitch.intro: Switching starts a new section. The past is not re-read.
categorySwitch.keep: Earlier raids, roster and quota stay readable as {from} (under {from} in the switch).
categorySwitch.new: From the save on, new raids are created as {to}.
categorySwitch.fresh: The attendance quota starts afresh, the {to} roster is new.

upcoming.one: 1 coming raid keeps its version. The orga may cancel it.
upcoming.other: {count} coming raids keep their version. The orga may cancel them.

categorySwitch.upcomingNone: No coming raids of another version.
categorySwitch.seriesMismatch: The series uses the template “{name}” ({version}). A template of another version creates no events.
categorySwitch.seriesFits: The series fits the new version.
categorySwitch.defaultMismatch: The default template “{name}” is {version} and no longer fits.
categorySwitch.noTemplates: There is no raid template for {to} yet – create one under Raid templates.
categorySwitch.rosterCloses: Roster “{name}” is closed. It stays readable under {from}, without sync with Discord – nobody loses a role.
categorySwitch.rosterExists: There already is the roster “{name}” for {to}.
categorySwitch.rosterCreateTip: With the name, managers, places and settings of the old roster.

rosterCopyTip.one: {count} person joins the new roster as trial, without a character – they pick their {to} character themselves.
rosterCopyTip.other: {count} people join the new roster as trial, without a character – each picks their {to} character themselves.

categorySwitch.rosterRoles: Discord roles of the new roster
categorySwitch.rosterRolesNone: No role picked: the new roster has no Discord role for now. Set it later in the roster's settings.

rosterRolesSome.one: {count} role picked. Nobody gets it automatically – the sync tab shows who lacks it.
rosterRolesSome.other: {count} roles picked. Nobody gets them automatically – the sync tab shows who lacks them.

rosterCreated.one: Roster “{name}” created for {version}, {count} person taken over
rosterCreated.other: Roster “{name}” created for {version}, {count} people taken over

drift.noneTip: All synced roles match their source role.
drift.tip: The sync only adds and never removes. Whoever lost the source role keeps the synced one until someone removes it in Discord.

overviewBadge.title: Raid overview
overviewBadge.notSetSub: Add a link with a channel for the overview under Discord servers.
overviewBadge.notPostedSub: It is posted on the next run (every 5 minutes) — or now with "Repost".
overviewBadge.currentSub: Updates on signups and sign-offs, new events and every 5 minutes.

dashboard.label: Overview
dashboard.description: Home page with key figures, upcoming and past events.

signup.label: Profile & signup
signup.description: Your own raider profile (characters, specs with gear state, availability, wishes) and your own signup for upcoming raids. Always only your own account.

recruitment.label: Recruitment
recruitment.description: Application templates and posted recruitment messages.

cla.label: CLA / Logcheck
cla.description: Start log evaluations, manage and assign reports.

raids.label: Raid events
raids.description: Create raid events, fill setups, post calls and Softres.

raidplan.label: Raid plan
raidplan.description: The raid plan on an event (boards per boss, posting the link), raid plan templates with tactic profiles and the raid plan catalog. An event's plan is opened through the event, which also takes reading raid events.

history.label: History & loot
history.description: Loot import, event and character history.

loot.label: Loot views
loot.description: Only the loot tabs of the history: imported loot, latest loot, loot reasons and items — without import, logs and raid lists.

lootcouncil.label: Loot council
lootcouncil.description: Caster overview for the loot council: awarded items per content, BiS gaps and upgrade suggestions.

kader.label: Roster planner
kader.description: Plan raid rosters for WoW Forever: player pool, a roster per raid, group setups. Assignments only apply inside the planner; the raider profile stays unchanged.

channels.label: Discord
channels.description: Create and duplicate Discord channels, post role messages. Also shows the member list of both servers with roster status and characters from all categories.

settings.label: Settings
settings.description: Bot configuration. Admin roles and permissions stay reserved for full admins.

ui.adminOnlySub: Roles with write access to "Settings" do not see this block and cannot save it.

fields.topItemsSub: When one of these items is imported, it shows up on the dashboard under "Latest Loot" — with character, raid and date. Without an entry the card stays empty.

raiderChars.title: Assign characters
raiderChars.noRoles: This category has no raider roles yet — pick roles in its row first and save.
raiderChars.noMembers: No members with the assigned roles found.

raidsheets.name: Name (content)
raidsheets.sheetIdSub: The long part of the sheet URL between /d/ and /edit.
raidsheets.gidSub: The number after #gid= in the tab's URL.
raidsheets.keywordsSub: Comma-separated. When a keyword matches the event title, this sheet is suggested automatically.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.tipSub: X hours before signup closes to everyone with a raider role who is still missing; Y hours before the raid starts to everyone signed up. Each reminder goes out exactly once and never after the raid has started. Without a signup deadline the raid start counts.
reminders.empty: No raid categories yet — they are switched on under Settings → Categories.
reminders.unknownCategorySub: Category ID {id} — not found (anymore) on any server of the list.
reminders.noRoleSub: Without a raider role for the category the bot does not know who is missing — the reminder to missing raiders then does not go out.
reminders.missingSub: Hours before signup closes (without a deadline: before the raid starts) to everyone with a raider role who has not reacted yet. Empty = off.
reminders.signedSub: Hours before the raid starts to everyone signed up (including "comes later"). Empty = off.
reminders.inactiveSub: The category is deactivated under Settings → Categories. The rule stays but reminds nobody until the category is active again.

roleSync.title: Role sync
roleSync.tipSub: Maps a role of one server to a role of another server of the list. Runs on every role change and every 10 minutes. It only adds and never removes.
roleSync.dirToTargetTip: Whoever has the role on the first server gets it on the second.
roleSync.dirToSourceTip: Whoever has the role on the second server gets it on the first.
roleSync.deleteText: Given roles stay as they are — the sync never removes anything.
roleSync.manageMissing: "Manage Roles" is missing on {servers} — the sync gives nothing there.
roleSync.empty: No mapping yet. Without a mapping no roles are given.
roleSync.notOnSource: No longer on the other server. Remove in Discord.
roleSync.lostSource: No longer has @{role}. Remove in Discord.
roleSync.directionSub: The sync only adds. A lost role stays on the other side and shows up as drift.
roleSync.fromServerTip: The server of the first role
roleSync.toServerTip: The server of the second role, another one than the first
roleSync.needTwo: The role sync needs at least two servers in the list.
roleSync.overlapTip: {both} members of {from} are on {to} as well. Only they can get the role there.

discordServers.tipSub: All servers are equal. A link posts one server's raid list to a channel on another server or the same one.
discordServers.linksSub: Where a server's raid list is posted. It updates on signups and sign-offs, new events and every 5 minutes.
discordServers.emptyLinks: No link yet — without a link the bot posts no raid list.
discordServers.removeLinkText: The raid list of {from} is no longer posted to {channel} on {to}.
discordServers.removeLinkInvite: Its invite is deleted on Discord.
discordServers.joinedTip: Members who came to the server through this invite
discordServers.signedUpTip: Of them, signed up for a raid of this server (absence does not count)
discordServers.regenerateSub: The old invite is deleted and stops working.
discordServers.regenerateText: The old invite is deleted on Discord. Wherever it was already shared, it leads nowhere afterwards.
discordServers.inviteDeleted: Invite deleted – create a new one?
discordServers.inviteChannelSub: Where people land who come through an invite of this server. Applies to newly created invites.
discordServers.generalInviteSub: An invite without a link, e.g. for your website. Anyone who comes through it counts for no link.
discordServers.serversSub: The servers the bot works with. A server without a raid category only shows other servers' lists.
discordServers.removeServerText: {name} is removed from the server list.

removeServerLinks.one: {count} link with this server as source is removed with it.
removeServerLinks.other: {count} links with this server as source are removed with it.

discordServers.removeServerInvites: The bot's invites on this server are deleted on Discord.
discordServers.emptyServers: No server yet — add the Discord your raids run on.
discordServers.noFreeServer: The bot is on no other server. Invite it there first.
discordServers.offlineText: No server list without a connection.
discordServers.label: Label
discordServers.labelSub: Optional extra title. The Discord name is always shown.
discordServers.sourceSub: The server whose raid list is posted.
discordServers.targetSub: The server the list appears on — the same server works too.
discordServers.channelSub: The channel on the target server.
discordServers.languageSub: Suggested is the target server's language. Server language = follows the target's Discord language.
discordServers.versionsSub: Only raids of these game versions. None chosen = all.
discordServers.noCategoryHint: {name} has no raid category yet. The list stays empty until one is created there.
discordServers.channelsSub: Apply to every server; the channel may be on any server.
discordServers.noteTipSub: Whoever presses "Tentative" or "Decline" in Discord can leave a short message for the raid lead — the bot posts it here. Whether it is asked (required, optional, none) you set per category under Categories.
discordServers.bankTipSub: The requests from the raid hub land here; empty = no guild bank button.

connections.discordSub: Whether the bot is connected and which Raid-Helper server supplies the events. Which servers are linked is set under Connections › Discord servers. The Raid-Helper API key itself stays in the .env.
connections.battlenetSub: Optional: with Battle.net API access the character history shows the live gear directly, and the loot council can use the Armory as a gear source.
connections.wclSub:
Draws raid DPS, raid HPS and boss health per boss fight in the fight timeline. Everything else in the log analysis keeps running on the v1 key in the .env.
The curves appear from the next evaluation on.
connections.aiSub: Claude words the recommendations from the log analysis in plain language for the raiders. The rules still decide what stood out; nothing goes out without approval.
connections.lootSyncSub: The WoW addon writes the loot from RCLootcouncil and Gargul into its SavedVariables; the sync tool on the raid leader's computer uploads it with one of these tokens. Uploaded raids land in History & loot → Addon inbox.
connections.discordMissing: The bot is not connected right now — server and role lists are missing until it is back online.
connections.raidhelperIdSub: Used for all Raid-Helper API calls (events, setups, signups). The API key itself stays in the .env.
connections.battlenetMissing: Without client ID and secret the character history shows no live gear.
connections.battlenetSecretSub: Never shown again. A new value replaces the stored secret.
connections.wclMissing: Without client ID and secret the fight timeline lacks the DPS, HPS and boss health curves.
connections.wclSecretSub: Create a client without a redirect URL under warcraftlogs.com/api/clients, leave "Public Client" off.
connections.aiMissing: Without an API key the recommendations stay with the rule texts.
connections.modelSub: Empty = claude-opus-5. The wording starts on the report page under "Recommendations".
connections.apiKeySub: Never shown again. A new value replaces the stored key.
connections.secretKeep: •••••••• stored — leave empty to keep it
connections.secretNote: Never shown again, only replaced or deleted.
connections.realmNotSet: per game version (main version has no realm)
connections.githubTip: GitHub token for the addon downloads
connections.githubSub: Reads the releases of the private addon repos (LevelHelper, ProfessionKit). Public repos work without it. The token never leaves the server, members download through the EventHelper.
connections.githubMissing: Without a token the page "Addons" shows the private addons as "not available right now".
connections.githubTokenSub: Create it on github.com under Settings > Developer settings > Fine-grained tokens: repository access "Only select repositories" with the addon repos, Permissions > Repository > Contents: "Read-only". Nothing else.

tokens.revokeText: The sync tool using it can no longer upload anything afterwards.
tokens.title: Loot sync tokens
tokens.created: Token "{name}" created — copy it now, the server only keeps a hash.
tokens.newSub: One name per computer, so a single one can be revoked on its own.
tokens.colTokenSub: The last four characters, so several tokens stay distinguishable.

permissions.orgaOnTip: {name} is an orga role – click to make it a raider role
permissions.orgaOffTip: {name} is a raider role – click to make it an orga role
permissions.orgaSub: Orga see the orga's parts (the dashboard's orga block, everybody's absences). An area only admins and orga roles open is marked “Orga area”. Which areas the role opens is set in its row, independently.
permissions.rowSub: Click: set the whole row to read, write or off
permissions.additiveSub: Whoever has several roles gets the sum of their permissions; base access and single accounts come on top and never take anything away. Changes apply to signed-in users within about 5 minutes.
permissions.additive: Permissions add up across all roles
permissions.adminsSub: Members with one of these roles have write access to every area and are the only ones with access to permissions and connection secrets. Changes apply within about 5 minutes without signing in again.
permissions.noRolesSub: Server chosen and bot online? The choice is available once the bot is connected.
permissions.emergencySub: The ADMIN_USER_ID from the .env always keeps full access, whatever is set here.
permissions.emergency: Emergency access via ADMIN_USER_ID always remains
permissions.baseSub: Applies to every Discord account that signs in — even without a role and without membership on the server. The menu with logout is always reachable; only what is unlocked here becomes visible.
permissions.rolesSub: Roles without admin rights get targeted access to single areas here. Read = view, write = act there too. Permissions and admin roles stay reserved for full admins — a role with write access to Settings cannot grant itself any rights.
permissions.rolesEmpty: No role with its own permissions yet — add one via "Role or account".
permissions.rolesNotLoaded: No roles loaded (server chosen and bot online?).
permissions.usersSub: Permissions for one specific Discord account — for areas that go to named people instead of a group (such as the loot council). Comes on top like the base access and never takes anything away.
permissions.roleAdminSub: Members with this role get full admin access.
permissions.roleGrantSub: The role starts without permissions; the cells of the new row unlock them.
permissions.discordIdSub: In Discord, right-click the user → "Copy ID" (developer mode must be on).
permissions.invalidId: That does not look like a Discord ID (17–20 digits).

categories.stillRhSub: New events of {names} are still created on Raid-Helper. To switch: open the category › New events. The switch-off checklist is under Connections › Raid-Helper.
categories.empty: No categories loaded (server chosen and bot online?). The list appears once the bot is connected.
categories.switchSub: Channels of this category hold raid events.
categories.unknownSub: This ID is configured, but Discord does not know it right now (bot offline?). Once the bot sees every server, a deleted category is marked “deleted in Discord” and can be closed.
categories.unprovenSub: Which Discord server this category belongs to is not proven — or its server is not in the server list. That is why it shows here and cannot be closed. Add the server under Discord servers and it moves there.
categories.charsSub: {assigned} of {members} raiders have a fixed character.
categories.raiderRolesSub: Whoever has one of these roles counts as an expected raider for raids of this category (attendance, missing signups, character assignment). Roles with "Raid" in their name are offered.
categories.noRaidRole: No role found whose name contains "Raid".
categories.charsDetailSub: Which character a raider plays in this category. Overrides the automatic detection from past signups on the event detail page.
categories.newEventsSub: Where new events of this category are created. Raid-Helper events stay in use either way – in lists, attendance, log and loot assignment.
categories.setupDmsSub: After release, every raider of an EventHelper event gets a DM: "You are in group 2 as a healer" or "Bench this time". On a new release only those whose spot changed get another one. The setup in the channel is always posted.
categories.languageSub: The bot writes everything a raid of this category posts in the channel in this language: signup message, setup, announcement, pings, Discord event. "As the server" takes the bot language of the general settings. What a raider reads personally (answers, DMs) stays in their own language.
categories.attendanceSub: Shows this category's attendance under Absences › My attendance – for the raiders themselves and for the orga. Off: the category does not appear there.
categories.attendanceWindowSub: How many of the last raids the attendance quota counts – in "My attendance" and in the setup editor's tooltip. Any whole number from 1 to 50, default: 11.
categories.absencesSub: This category's raids and absences that only apply to it appear in the timeline, under "Per raid" and in the hints. Off: the category stays out of it.
categories.announceSub: A new EventHelper event posts a short line with title, date and signup link and pings the raider roles of this category — exactly once per event, series events included.
categories.notesSub: Whoever presses "Tentative" or "Decline" in Discord gets a field for a short message to the raid lead. The bot posts it in the channel you pick under Connections › Discord servers — or below in one of this category's own. "none" does not ask and posts nothing.
categories.noteChannelSub: Where this category's messages go. "Default" is the channel under Connections › Discord servers. A channel the bot can no longer reach falls back to the default.
categories.unreachableSub: The bot does not see this channel (anymore) or may not write there. Messages go to the default channel meanwhile.
categories.discordEventSub: For every EventHelper event of this category the bot creates a Discord event (server sidebar, mobile app). It follows moves, cancellations and deletions. Signup still runs only through the message in the channel — "Interested" does not count. The bot needs the "Manage Events" permission for it.
categories.raidArtSub: Below the signup message there is a picture of the raid (Blizzard's zone picture of the evening's largest instance). An event with its own banner keeps it.
categories.titleSizeSub: How large the letter tiles of the title in the signup message are. "very large" wraps a long title into two lines sooner.
categories.voiceSub: Where the raids of this category meet. Preset when creating an event — still changeable there. Shown in the signup message and the location of the Discord event.
categories.lootAddonSub: Preselects the matching parser on loot import and tells the loot tab of the raid detail page which export to expect.
categories.lootSystemSub: Decides what a raid of this category offers: only with Softres is there the Softres step, "Softres missing" and the Softres list in the menu. "automatic" = {auto}. Single raids can be switched on their page or have Softres added.
categories.templateSub: The raid template a new event of this category starts from. While it is the default it cannot be deleted. You maintain templates under Raid events › Raid templates.
categories.fixedSheetSub: Every raid of this category links this sheet — unless one was created for the raid itself. Templates by keyword: Modules › Raidsheets.
categories.noneShown: No raid category yet — switch on a Discord category below.

folded.one: {count} more Discord category without raid events
folded.other: {count} more Discord categories without raid events

categories.panelSub: A Discord message for this category's raiders: next raid, absence and attendance, their own evaluation and your links. Posting again replaces the old message.
categories.panelRemoveText: The message in Discord is deleted. What raiders already entered stays.
categories.panelNoChannels: No text channels – is the bot online?
categories.orgaHubSub: A Discord message for the orga: the raids of the next 4 weeks, where each one stands, and “Create raid”. Post it into a channel only the orga sees.
categories.orgaHubChannelAria: Channel for the orga hub of {name}
categories.orgaHubRemoveText: The message in Discord is deleted. The raids themselves stay as they are.
categories.orgaLinksSub: Buttons below “Create raid”, e.g. the WCL guild or raid sheet – for the orga only. Also editable in Discord through “Links …” on the orga hub.
categories.linksSub: Buttons such as the WCL invite, info sheet or tactics – shown at the bottom of the panel.
categories.planningSub: How the raids of this category are assigned: raid plan (one board per boss, "Assignments" in the channel) or Google Sheet (the fixed sheet, or a copy of a template per raid). Never both. Without a pick: a fixed sheet means sheet, otherwise raid plan.
categories.planningRaidplanSub: Raid page with the "Raid plan" tab and the "Assignments" step; no raidsheet.
categories.planningCopiesSub: No fixed sheet: each raid fills a copy of a raidsheet template (Modules › Raidsheets).
categories.attendanceBlockShort: Show it, count it, include it in absences.
categories.attendanceShort: For the raiders themselves and for the orga.
categories.attendanceWindowShort: This many of the last raids count. Default: 11.
categories.raiderRolesShort: Whoever has one of these roles is expected at the raids.
categories.charsShort: A fixed character per raider instead of automatic detection.
categories.templateShort: A new event starts from this template.
categories.voiceShort: Preset, still changeable on the event.
categories.announceShort: Pings the raider roles once per event.
categories.discordEventShort: Also an event in the server sidebar.
categories.languageShort: For everything posted in the channel.
categories.raidArtShort: Zone picture below the signup message.
categories.titleSizeShort: Size of the title's letter tiles.
categories.notesShort: A short message to the raid lead.
categories.panelShort: For raiders: next raid, absence and attendance, your links.
categories.orgaHubShort: For the orga: raids of the next 4 weeks and "Create raid".
categories.planningShort: Raid plan or Google Sheet, never both.
categories.fixedSheetShort: Every raid of this category links this sheet.
categories.setupDmsShort: Every raider learns their spot by DM.
categories.lootSystemShort: Decides what a raid of this category offers.
categories.lootAddonShort: Which export the loot import expects.

tabsIntro.raider: Who belongs to this category – and how their attendance is counted.
tabsIntro.events: What happens when a new event of this category is created.
tabsIntro.message: How signing up looks – the message in the channel, what its buttons ask and how many characters it takes.
tabsIntro.hubs: This category's standing Discord messages – one for the raiders, one for the orga.
tabsIntro.plan: What the raids are assigned with and who hears about it after the release.
tabsIntro.loot: How loot is handed out and imported in this category.

categories.signupCharsShort: How many characters a raider may name in one signup — the first counts, the others are “can also come with”.
categories.signupCharsSub: Applies everywhere: the signup dialog on the web, the signup message in Discord and “Several raids”. 1 to 8, default: 8. Whoever is already signed up with more characters keeps them – they can take some out, but not add any.

modeTip.everyone: Every member may use the command.
modeTip.roles: Only members with one of the chosen roles (on the first server of the list).
modeTip.admins: Admins only: ADMIN_USER_ID and the admin roles from "Access".

botCommands.unknownRoleSub: Role ID {id} — no longer exists on the first server.
botCommands.title: Bot commands
botCommands.tipSub: Who may use which command in Discord. Buttons and selects of a command inherit its permission. Admins may always do everything.
botCommands.loadError: Could not load the bot commands: {message}
botCommands.noRoles: No roles loaded — is the bot online and a server listed?
botCommands.savedGroup: Saved for all commands of the group.
botCommands.rolesSub: Roles of the first server of the list. Whoever has one of them may use the command.
botCommands.wholeGroup: apply to all {count} commands of the group

guildBanks.title: Guild banks
guildBanks.infoSub: The EventHelper addon scans the guild bank, the sync tool uploads the scan. A bank belongs to a server: with just one server it lands there by itself, otherwise it waits here for the assignment.
guildBanks.deleteText: The bank and everything set for its items (sorting, reserve, limit) are deleted. The next scan creates it anew.
guildBanks.unassigned: {name} is waiting for the assignment again.

rhSync.title: Raid-Helper sync
rhSync.infoSub: The pages never ask Raid-Helper for events themselves. One job fetches the list every {minutes} minutes with a single request, and every page reads that copy. Raid-Helper allows 1000 requests a day.
rhSync.budgetSub: This many requests went to Raid-Helper in the last 24 hours. At {cap} the bot stops by itself, so Raid-Helper's limit is never reached.
rhSync.throttled: Just synced, try again in 30 seconds.

retirement.title: Switching from Raid-Helper
retirement.optionalTip: Recommendation – switching off does not depend on it.
retirement.switchDisabled: Raid-Helper is no longer queried. The history stays readable; switching back on works any time.
retirement.switchReady: All required items done. Switching off stops all requests to Raid-Helper; past raids stay readable.
retirement.importNothingNew: Nothing new – {count} events are already imported.
retirement.importDry: {events} events · {entries} entries for {users} raiders would be saved.
retirement.whatSub: Only who signed up with which spec – no events, no signups. From that, the one-click signup and the profile suggest the spec played last. An event is never counted twice; a second import only fetches new raids.
retirement.dryFirst: Only the dry run shows what would be saved. Nothing is saved until "Import".
retirement.liveText: Raid-Helper does not answer – only the stored events were read.
retirement.skippedSub: These events were counted in an earlier import and are skipped.
retirement.offText: The EventHelper then no longer queries Raid-Helper: no new Raid-Helper events, no signups, no scan. Past raids stay readable with their stored signups. Switching back on works any time.
retirement.onText: Events, signups and the scan then run through Raid-Helper again.
retirement.infoSub: What should be done before the EventHelper replaces Raid-Helper completely. The two required items unlock the switch below; the rest makes the raiders' everyday life easier. Each item explains itself in the tooltip of its name.

versionLinks.title: Links and armory per version
versionLinks.titleSub: Where a character is looked up (armory, Warcraft Logs) and where items link to (Wowhead), separately for every game version. An event uses the values of its version, raider pages and the loot council those of the main version or the category.
versionLinks.colorSub: The accent colour of the web admin (buttons, active menu line, links, selection) while this version is shown. The version's name always stays visible in the switch at the top. Empty = the version's standard colour. Settings, Channels and System status keep the brand colour.
versionLinks.emptyHint: These values apply only to {version}. Empty field = the link is left out.
versionLinks.namespaceSub: Profile namespace of the Blizzard API, e.g. profile-classicann-eu for TBC Anniversary. Empty = no armory lookup for this version.
versionLinks.templateSub: An address with {char} where the character name goes; {region} and {realm} insert the region and realm from above. Empty = no link.
versionLinks.wowheadSub: The part after wowhead.com/, e.g. tbc or classic. Empty = no Wowhead links and no item search.
versionLinks.softresSub: Which edition softres.it uses for this version. None = no softres for events of this version.
versionLinks.raidsheetSub: The raidsheet of an event of this version when no keyword matches. A raidsheet of another version is never picked by keyword.

invalid.blizzardRealmSlug: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens only.
invalid.blizzardNamespace: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens only.
invalid.wowheadPath: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens only, e.g. tbc.

versionLinks.defaultsSub: Fills in the known values for {version} (namespace, armory, Warcraft Logs, Wowhead, softres). Realm and raidsheet stay as they are. Nothing is stored until you save.
versionLinks.defaultsSame: The standard values are already filled in.
versionLinks.defaultsNone: No standard values are known for {version} yet.

versionFeatures.title: Features per version
versionFeatures.titleSub: What each game version can do. A feature is possible when data, rules or settings exist for the version. Only then is there a switch. Stored with “Save”.
versionFeatures.onSub: Switched on. Off behaves like “not possible”.

featureSub.lootCouncilBis: BiS lists, item table and tier filter in the loot council.
featureSub.simulation: DPS simulation (WoWSims) in the loot council.
featureSub.raidSheet: Filling the Google raid sheet. Without it the raid plans with the raid plan.
featureSub.softres: Creating a softres list on the raid page.
featureSub.armory: Fetching gear and character data from Battle.net.
featureSub.wowheadLinks: Links to Wowhead for items and spells.
featureSub.raidplanCatalog: The catalog's mobs and spells in the raid plan.
featureSub.dungeonTimes: Dungeon best times from the LevelHelper addon per character in "My profile".

reason.rules_not_ready: Log check rules for {version} not finished yet ({count} open).
reason.no_site: No Warcraft Logs site set for {version}.
reason.armory_not_configured: Armory for {version} not set up (region, realm, namespace).
reason.no_dungeon_times: No dungeon best times for {version} (no LevelHelper).

versionLaunch.title: Start a new version
versionLaunch.titleSub: What should be done on the switch day, per target version. The state comes from the real data. Only what cannot be checked is ticked off by hand. Details in each item's tooltip.
versionLaunch.optionalTip: Only when the old version ends for good. Not counted.
versionLaunch.manualTip: Cannot be checked from the data: tick it off yourself.

backup.label: Data backed up
backup.why: A fresh backup before the switch: if something goes wrong, today's state can be brought back.

export.label: Archive of the old version downloaded
export.why: Loot and attendance of every version but the main one as CSV. Worth it when the old version ends: download it after switching the main version.

categories.label: Every category has a fixed version
categories.why: Every active category plays exactly one version. A switch starts a new section, old raids stay in their version.

versionSettings.label: Links of the version set
versionSettings.why: Realm, armory, Warcraft Logs, Wowhead, softres and raid sheet of the target version. Empty is fine where the feature is not possible for the version or switched off.

templates.label: Raid templates of the version exist
templates.why: New raids, series and a category's default template need templates of this version.

series.label: Series and default templates fit
series.why: A template of another version creates no event. The series would fail.

rosters.label: Rosters with roles and managers
rosters.why: Every category of the version needs an open roster with Discord roles and managers. Rosters exist per version.

guildBank.label: Guild bank assigned
guildBank.why: The new version's bank arrives with the first scan from the game and needs a Discord server.

lootAddon.label: Loot addon tested on the new client
lootAddon.why: Record loot and a bank scan once on the new client and upload them. Does the version arrive correctly?

talk.label: Raid lists and reminders checked
talk.why: The raid lists of the links and the reminders show raids of every version. Take a look whether the new raids appear correctly.

mainVersion.label: Main version switched, others hidden
mainVersion.why: Only when the old version ends for good: switch the main version to the new one and turn on “Hide other versions”.

detail.noTarget: No active category plays {version}. Switch a category first.
detail.backupManual: This instance takes no backup of its own: back up by hand and tick it off.

botLanguage.label: Bot language
botLanguage.text: Language of the bot's public messages (signup message, setup, overview, panels) and the default for every raider. Everyone can pick their own language with /language or the DE/EN switch at the top.

categoryDeactivate.intro: Nothing is deleted. What runs on its own pauses until the category is active again.

upcoming.one: 1 upcoming raid stays, without reminders. The organisers can cancel it.
upcoming.other: {count} upcoming raids stay, without reminders. The organisers can cancel them.

categoryDeactivate.keep: Settings, rosters, raids, loot and logs stay. The squad planner, the roster picker and /anwesenheit no longer offer the category; archive and history still show it. Activating it again resumes everything.
categoryDeactivate.emptyBlocked: At least one raid category must stay active while there are raids.

categoryClose.badgeSub: This category no longer exists in Discord. “Close category” cleans up its settings; raids, loot and logs stay readable under their version.
categoryClose.saveFirst: Save or discard the open changes first.
categoryClose.title: Close {name}
categoryClose.intro: The category was deleted in Discord. Closing removes what only new raids need:

removeSettings.one: 1 category setting is removed (roles, template, channels …).
removeSettings.other: {count} category settings are removed (roles, template, channels …).

categoryClose.removeActive: It is no longer a raid category.
categoryClose.removeCouncil: Its Loot Council profile entry is removed.

removeKaders.one: It no longer counts for attendance in the squad {names}.
removeKaders.other: It no longer counts for attendance in {count} squads: {names}.

upcoming.one: 1 upcoming raid is still in the category – please cancel it.
upcoming.other: {count} upcoming raids are still in the category – please cancel them.

categoryClose.rosters: These rosters belong to the category and are closed: they stay readable under their version, without sync with Discord – nobody loses a role. A full admin can delete them later on the roster page.
categoryClose.keep: What stays: raids, loot, logs and the category's version and name – everything stays readable under its version.

discordVisuals.label: Pictures in bot messages
discordVisuals.text: Test: the bot draws parts of its messages as a picture. Off = the text form as before, from the message's next update.
discordVisuals.overviewWeekStripTip: Test: each ID's week as a picture above its raids in the raid overview (/createoverview).
discordVisuals.setupImageTip: Test: the groups of the posted setup as a picture instead of a list; confirm marks in the picture, the buttons stay.
discordVisuals.eventCoverTip: Test: a raid's Discord server event gets the raid's picture as its cover (the event's own picture, else the zone art).

dungeonRecords.postTip: A gold run that is now the fastest of its dungeon goes into the channel as a card. Only runs of the last three days, at most three per upload.
dungeonRecords.channelSub: The bot posts every new guild record here, in the bot language.
dungeonRecords.noChannel: Without a channel nothing is posted.
